title: Redundant Link Identification in Quasi-Trees
description: A graph was originally a tree with n nodes labeled 1 to n, but one additional edge was added, creating exactly one cycle. Given the list of n edges, find the one edge that, if removed, would restore the tree structure. If there are multiple such edges, choose the one that appears last in the input.
input_format:
The first line contains two integers n and c (number of nodes and a constant 2).
The next n lines each contain two integers u and v, representing an undirected edge between nodes u and v.
output_format: Print two space-separated integers representing the redundant edge discovered in the input. If multiple edges could be removed, print the one that occurs latest in the list.
constraints:
3 <= n <= 1000
1 <= u, v <= n
There are no repeated edges.
The given graph is connected.
